summary: Paul Tedesco was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), held a post at Princeton (~1938–1944), and served as a professor at Yale University (1952–1966).

Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Hermann, Sieg, Andreas, Schulze, Lüders, and Mishra. His career included posts at Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau, holding professorships at Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976) and served as Associate Professor of Chinese and chairman of Oriental Languages and Literatures at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1980).

Paul Williams is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Sussex and Oxford, was Bowra Research Fellow at Wadham College, and later served as Emeritus Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at the University of Bristol (~1980–2011).

Paul de Lagarde was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg under Friedrich Rückert and held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1853) and the University of Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula Arai works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Kalamazoo College, Waseda, and Harvard under Nagatomi and Smith. She has held posts at Vanderbilt, LSU, Carleton College, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio. He served in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and later held posts in Rome in 1800.
Pavankumar Satuluri works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (attested 2024–2025).

Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the universities of Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Professor of Pali and Principal at the University of Rangoon (1912; 1937–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. She studied at National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Donald F. McCallum.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa and others, serving as director and abbess of Gampo Abbey beginning in 1984.
Pema Donyo Nyinje is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Pema Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke (attested 2026).
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
